name: Delayed damage bar
summary: When health drops, a pale bar stays where the health was for a moment and then drains, showing how big the hit was.
what_it_does: An instant drop in a health bar is easy to miss, and it doesn't show how much one hit took. Keeping a second, lighter bar at the old value for a short time and then draining it makes the size of the loss visible after the fact.
watch_out: Game logic and low-health warnings should read the real value, never the pale one.
starting_values: No checked source gives timings. Hold for 300 to 700 ms, then drain over a similar time, as a starting point.
prompt:
Add a delayed damage bar behind the health bar.
- Keep ghostHealth. When health drops, leave ghostHealth where it was.
- 500 ms after the last hit, move ghostHealth toward health at 2 health points per second.
- When health goes up, set ghostHealth to it right away.
- Draw ghostHealth as a pale bar behind the real one.

Acceptance checks:
1. After a hit, the pale part shows the size of the loss for 500 ms.
2. Several quick hits extend the pale part instead of resetting it.
3. Healing never shows a pale part.
